Word Cloud Generation Logic
The vocabulary was built through a systematic three-phase expansion process:

Phase 1: Seed Selection
12 foundational terms were chosen as anchors, emphasizing:

Action-oriented verbs (Prompt, Swap, Morph)

Structural concepts (Node, Network, Hub)

Transformation states (Alter, Convert, Merge)

Technology anchors (AI, Neural, Algorithm)

Phase 2: Lexical Expansion
Each seed word underwent three-dimensional branching:

Synonym Layer

Direct meaning equivalents (e.g., "Create" → Generate, Fabricate)

Thesaurus-derived with preference for active verbs

Contextual Layer

Associated tools/objects (e.g., "Node" → Router, Server)

Process-related terms (e.g., "Modify" → Adjust, Revise)

Combinatorial Layer

Pre-broken hyphenation points (e.g., "Stim-ulate")

Phonetically viable fragments for portmanteaus

Phase 3: Phonetic Filtering
Potential word pairs were evaluated against:

Pronounceability Test

Valid: "Net-graph" (natural syllabic flow)

Rejected: "Algo-rithm" (awkward fragment)

Semantic Cohesion

Hybrids required loose thematic relevance

Non-sequiturs like "Face-book" were manually approved for creative potential

Final Curation Criteria
The cloud prioritized:

Motion-capable words (nouns with verb potential)

Modularity indicators (terms implying connectivity)

Visualizability (concrete over abstract concepts)

Exclusion Rules:

Single-syllable words without pairing flexibility

Overly niche jargon lacking broad applicability

Static terms without transformational connotations

Resulting Lexicon Properties
Category	% of Cloud	Example Words
Action Verbs	38%	Merge, Provoke, Reconfigure
System Nouns	35%	Hub, Pathway, Intersection
State Changers	22%	Mutate, Regenerate, Adapt
Tech Primitives	5%	Neural, Modular, Cognitive
Implementation Notes
Depth Stratification

Foreground: Action verbs (larger, brighter)

Background: Structural terms (smaller, hazed)

Pairing Mechanics

Magnetic attraction strength varies by:

Phonetic compatibility (measured via syllable stress patterns)

Semantic proximity (pre-calculated word2vec similarity)

This methodology produced a self-referential word ecosystem optimized for both visual dynamism and meaningful recombination potential. The system remains extensible for new semantic domains through consistent application of the three-phase protocol.
